dna.fixture_why: The artifact stands as the whole ladder by default, which is what it is for. The SWEEP must see one rung at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so an all-rungs view in the same spec frames every single rung against a row several times its width and photographs it as a speck. That is not a hypothetical - it crashed the critic on a subject box too small to sample.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 31.1% of frame width and 30.7% of its height, with a subject share of 7.45%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.39. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.

frequency_shell.description: Four geodesic domes at the frequencies the family's five members all declare - v1 to v4 - with each dome's distinct strut lengths laid out beneath it as real struts of those real lengths. The shape converges and the parts list diverges, which is the cost nobody in the family shows.
